proposed.text: An architect created a distinctive building design. Five years later, without authorization, another firm constructed an identical building using the same floor plans and facade design. What is the most appropriate civil remedy for the architect to seek?

options.text: A preliminary injunction to stop further infringing use or construction, plus monetary relief subject to RA 8293 proof and damages-limit rules
Automatic criminal prosecution for theft, without needing Section 217 facts
Automatic demolition of the completed building as the ordinary remedy
Damages only; injunctive relief is never available once construction is complete

rationale.b: Criminal penalties require a separate Section 217 analysis.
rationale.c: The local source supports disposal/destruction of infringing copies and devices, but not automatic demolition as the ordinary answer.
rationale.correct: RA 8293 Section 186 covers erection of a building reproducing a protected architectural work. Section 216 includes injunction and damages/profits remedies. Section 226 limits damages recovery after four years from the time the cause of action arose, so the source-safe civil remedy is injunction plus monetary relief subject to proof and timing limits.
rationale.takeaway: Civil remedies under RA 8293 can include injunction and money relief, but damages must respect Section 226.
